title: Discussion & debate
examples: How do I respond if someone says something I disagree with?
What is the best way to keep my side of the argument clear?
Can you give me some phrases for starting a disagreement politely?

explain.say: Today we learn how to join a discussion well. Learning to take turns helps everyone speak. You must wait for a pause before you begin to talk.

items: Raise hand or wait to speak

explain.say: A concrete example of turn-taking is in a classroom discussion. When the teacher asks a question, one student answers first. Then another student can add their thoughts next.
Next we learn about rebuttal. A rebuttal means you reply to a point made. You must show why that point is incorrect or weak.

draw.text: Rebuttal: Reply to a specific point.

explain.say: For example, if someone says all phones are bad, you can rebut that. You can say phones are useful for learning and safety.

draw.text: Rebuttal: Phones are useful for learning.

explain.say: Our final skill is respectful disagreement. You must disagree with the idea, not the person. Keep your tone calm and polite always.
In real life, you use this when deciding on a group project theme. One person suggests history, but you must respectfully disagree and suggest science instead.

faq.q: How do I start my rebuttal without sounding aggressive?
faq.a: You can start by saying, 'I see your point, but I think...' This shows you listened first. You could also say, 'While that is true, we should also consider...'

faq.q: Is it okay to interrupt someone if I have a very important point?
faq.a: It is best to wait for a natural pause. If you must interrupt, use a very polite phrase like, 'Excuse me, may I add something quickly?'
asks: What if I can't wait to speak?

faq.q: What is the difference between disagreeing and attacking a person?
faq.a: Disagreeing is about the facts or the idea presented. Attacking is criticizing the person's character or intelligence. Always stick to the idea.
asks: When is it rude to disagree?
How do I keep it personal vs. academic?

faq.q: Should I use strong words to make my point heard?
faq.a: No, strong words can sound aggressive. Use strong evidence and clear, confident language instead. Your evidence is your strength.
asks: Is passion enough for a good argument?

faq.q: What if everyone on my side agrees with each other?
faq.a: You can still introduce a new angle or ask a 'what if' question. This forces the group to think about possibilities they missed.
asks: How do I challenge my own team?
What if my side is too strong?

facts: Turn-taking involves listening actively to the speaker.
A rebuttal directly addresses a previous statement.
Respectful disagreement focuses on the argument, not the person.
Using 'I believe' helps own your perspective.

quiz.say: If someone says that all art is subjective, and you want to rebut, which response is best?

options.show: Art is only good if it sells well.
options.say: Art is only good if it sells well.

options.show: You are wrong to think art is subjective.
options.say: You are wrong to think art is subjective.

options.show: I disagree completely with your entire point.
options.say: I disagree completely with your entire point.

options.show: While art is subjective, historical records show specific techniques.
options.say: While art is subjective, historical records show specific techniques.

quiz.why: This answer acknowledges the opponent's point but introduces factual limitations.

wrong.0: This is an extreme generalization and doesn't address the concept of subjectivity.
wrong.1: This attacks the person rather than the idea, which is disrespectful.
wrong.2: This is too vague; it does not specifically rebut the idea presented.

quiz.say: When you are in a group discussion, what is the first thing you should do before speaking?

options.show: Wait for a clear pause or invitation to speak.
options.say: Wait for a clear pause or invitation to speak.

options.show: Interrupt immediately with my best point.
options.say: Interrupt immediately with my best point.

options.show: Wait until the discussion ends completely.
options.say: Wait until the discussion ends completely.

quiz.why: Waiting shows you are listening and respecting the flow of conversation.

wrong.0: Loudness does not equal good argumentation; tone matters more.
wrong.2: Interrupting breaks the flow and shows poor listening skills.
wrong.3: Waiting too long means you lose your chance to contribute to the topic.

quiz.say: Which phrase helps you disagree respectfully?

options.show: That is absolutely false and incorrect.
options.say: That is absolutely false and incorrect.

options.show: You must be mistaken about that fact.
options.say: You must be mistaken about that fact.

options.show: I see your point, however, I wonder if...
options.say: I see your point, however, I wonder if...

quiz.why: This structure validates the other person before introducing a counter-thought.

wrong.0: This is too confrontational and lacks the required respect.
wrong.1: This directly questions the person's knowledge, which is impolite.
wrong.2: This is an absolute statement that shuts down further discussion.
